tagline: The first parkway to break ground, not the first to open.
intro: From the rotary below Kensico Dam the parkway follows the Bronx River south through the Bronx River Reservation, Westchester County's first park, with Metro-North's Harlem Line alongside most of the way. North of White Plains the crossings are at traffic lights. Below the Sprain Brook junction it becomes a fully controlled-access commuter road and runs on into the Bronx, but only the Westchester part is the byway.

Construction began here in 1907, the first limited-access motor road in the country to break ground. Long Island's Motor Parkway, begun a year later, opened first. This one was the first highway with a median strip, the first built through a park and the first to carry the crossing streets over on bridges.

moments.title: Kensico Dam
moments.text: The parkway starts within sight of the dam, 307 feet high and finished in 1917, three years ahead of schedule, for a reservoir that flooded the village of Kensico.

moments.title: White Plains
moments.text: In the county seat the road crosses the river and the tracks, and near the expressway its two roadways drift almost 400 feet apart before meeting again.

moments.title: Yonkers
moments.text: In Yonkers, past Leewood Drive, the two roadways divide and the Bronx River runs between them through a wooded stretch.
